replacements.before: The finite-sector results have broad mathematical strength, but several tempting extensions lie outside their conclusions. A statement about the span of an algebra orbit permits every matrix in that algebra; it does not say a physically specified unitary gate set reaches every vector. replacements.after: The finite results have broad mathematical scope, but their hypotheses also place clear limits on their use. A statement about the span of an algebra orbit permits every matrix in that algebra. Reachability under a physically specified set of unitary gates requires a separate argument. A theorem establishing complete positivity for finite channels quantifies over every finite reference index. Arbitrary infinite reference Hilbert spaces lie outside those declarations.

replacements.before: This chain explains the division among the six projected-geometry files. \code{ProjectedCurvature} establishes the parameter-space algebra and calculus; \code{LocalProjectedCurvature} localizes the hypotheses; \code{GlobalRangeBundle} constructs the atlas; \code{GlobalProjectedConnection} defines and glues the connection; \code{ManifoldProjectedCurvature} proves the actual global curvature formula; \code{ProjectedBundleCompletion} supplies intrinsic section, gauge and fiber-form compatibility. Treating only the earliest chart file as current coverage would miss the later global constructions.
replacements.after: The six files on projected geometry follow this mathematical development. \code{ProjectedCurvature} establishes the algebra and calculus on the parameter space. \code{LocalProjectedCurvature} makes the hypotheses local, and \code{GlobalRangeBundle} constructs the atlas. \code{GlobalProjectedConnection} defines the connection and proves that its local descriptions agree. \code{ManifoldProjectedCurvature} proves the global curvature formula. Finally, \code{ProjectedBundleCompletion} proves compatibility with intrinsic sections, gauge transformations and the curvature form on each fiber. The later global constructions extend the results of the earliest chart file.
